## 1. Infrastructure Overview & Scope
<a id="laminar-sec-g.1"></a>
The DataOutbound Product is provisioned as a single AWS-based, event-driven batch data-egress platform within the hospitality data platform domain. All pipeline-owned infrastructure is deployed in **one Terraform root module** (`terraform/main.tf`) covering:

| Service type | Components provisioned |
|---|---|
| API compute (ECS Fargate behind an ALB) | do-admin-api (REST, JWT) |
| EventBridge | scheduler (rule `scheduler`) |
| MWAA (Apache Airflow) | orchestrator, child_export_dag, egress dag (one MWAA environment hosts all three DAGs) |
| EMR Serverless | emr_do (Spark, emr-7.0.0) |
| Redshift | dev (cluster `golden_data_source`) — externally owned source, consumed read-only |
| RDS Postgres | cofig_db |
| S3 | staging_bucet_internal, audit_bucket |
| Lambda | egress-lambda |
| External / customer-owned (not provisioned) | customer SFTP server, customer bucket, Customer Azure Blob Destination, Customer GCS Destination |

**Multi-environment scope**: `dev`, `staging`, `prod` workspaces of the same root module, driven entirely by `values.yaml` per environment. Per SCRUM-485, deletion-protection flags for all stateful resources (`export_config_store_rds`, `customer_staging_buckets_s3`, `audit_execution_log_store_s3`, and the KMS key) are read from the per-environment variable `deletion_protection_enabled` — `false` in dev (clean teardown), `true` in staging and prod — with zero hardcoded values in the module.

**Region strategy**: single primary region (default `us-east-1`, overridable via `values.yaml`); all components co-located to minimise cross-AZ latency. The Golden Entity Source Store (`dev` Redshift) is an existing externally owned cluster; the pipeline consumes it read-only and never provisions or modifies it. Customer destinations are customer-owned; this specification defines only our side of each delivery contract.

**RPO/RTO targets**: cofig_db RPO 24 h / RTO 2 h (automated backups, snapshot retention 30 days); staging_bucet_internal is ephemeral (7-day purge, no backup required); audit_bucket is append-only telemetry with lifecycle tiering (30 d → Glacier at 90 d).

## 2. IaaC Tenets & Automation Principles
<a id="laminar-sec-g.2"></a>
1. **Single root module, environment overlays.** One Terraform root module (`main.tf`, `variables.tf`, `values.yaml`, one `<service>.tf` per service type: `api.tf`, `blob_store.tf`, `emr.tf`, `eventbridge.tf`, `gcs.tf`, `lambda.tf`, `mwaa.tf`, `rds.tf`, `redshift.tf`, `s3.tf`). No nested modules with hidden defaults; every environment-specific value lives in `values.yaml`.
2. **Immutability & declarative state.** All resources are managed declaratively; no manual console changes. Stateful resources (RDS, S3 buckets, KMS keys) carry `prevent_destroy` guarded by the `deletion_protection_enabled` variable so dev teardown succeeds while staging/prod teardown fails closed (SCRUM-485 AC#4/AC#5).
3. **Secure-by-default.** Every S3 bucket ships with public-access block and SSE; every database enforces TLS; every IAM role is least-privilege with explicit ARNs (no wildcards on resources); secrets never appear in code or state plaintext — resolved at runtime from SSM Parameter Store (SecureString).
4. **Environment parity.** Identical module code across dev/staging/prod; only `values.yaml` differs (sizing, deletion protection, retention, feature flags). Lower environments remain fully teardown-compatible.
5. **Automated verification.** `terraform plan` gates with policy checks (allowlist of MWAA, RDS Postgres, Lambda, EMR Serverless, S3, ECS per SCRUM-485 AC#1), `terraform validate`/`fmt` in CI, and a post-apply inventory check that exits non-zero on any out-of-allowlist resource.
6. **Explicit observability provisioning.** Log groups are created explicitly per component with a single organisation retention value (`log_retention_days` variable — value to be confirmed per SCRUM-486; never unset or never-expire), plus CloudWatch alarms defined in Terraform.

### 6.1. Infrastructure Specification: do-admin-api
<a id="laminar-sec-g.6.imp_standard_standard_api_1"></a>

<!-- laminar:diagram-settings:imp-standard-standard_api-1 -->
**Diagram settings (user decisions — authoritative)**

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `protocol` | `REST` |
| `authentication` | `JWT` |
| `api_name` | `do-admin-api` |

<!-- /laminar:diagram-settings -->

#### 6.1.1 Resource Configuration & Sizing

| Parameter | Value | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| api_name | `do-admin-api` | User-set (authoritative) |
| protocol / authentication | REST / JWT | User-set (authoritative) |
| Terraform resource | `export_admin_api` (in `terraform/api.tf`) | Blueprint |
| Compute | ECS Fargate task, 1 vCPU / 2048 MB, desired count 1 (dev) / 2 (staging, prod) | Low-latency control plane (<500 ms CRUD); 2 tasks in higher envs for AZ redundancy |
| Container image | `python:3.11-slim` base, app from `src/dataoutbound_st_fixes/apis/export_admin_api` | Blueprint language python |
| ALB | internet-facing ALB, HTTPS:443 listener, TLS 1.3 policy `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06` | Zero-trust transport guardrail |
| Scaling | target-tracking on `ALBRequestCountPerTarget` = 200, min 1, max 4 | Bounded burst absorption without over-provisioning |
| DB connection pooling | max 10 connections per task | db.t3.micro `cofig_db` has limited connection budget |
| Log group | `/laminar/dataoutbound/do-admin-api/{env}`, retention = `log_retention_days` variable | SCRUM-486 AC#4 (value confirmed before sprint commitment) |

#### 6.1.2 IAM Role & Policies

Task execution role (ECR pull, logs) is standard; the task role below carries least-privilege app permissions. Note: `rds-db:connect` is intentionally **not** granted — the API connects to `cofig_db` over Postgres TLS with credentials resolved from SSM (SecureString), not RDS IAM DB auth; SSM access is read-only on the component's own path only (no `ssm:PutParameter`).

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "ReadDbCredentialsFromSsm",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["ssm:GetParameter", "ssm:GetParameters"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ssm:${region}:${account}:parameter/laminar/dataoutbound/${env}/do-admin-api/*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "TriggerOrchestratorViaMwaaRestApi",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["airflow:CreateApiToken", "airflow:InvokeRestApi"],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:airflow:${region}:${account}:environment/laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-${env}",
        "arn:aws:airflow:${region}:${account}:environment/laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-${env}#dags/orchestrator"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Sid": "WriteAuditEvents",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:PutObject"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket/admin/*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "KmsDecryptForSecrets",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:${region}:${account}:key/${laminar_dataoutbound_key_id}"
    }
  ]
}
```

Trust policy (ECS tasks):

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": { "Service": "ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com" },
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
    "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:SourceAccount": "${account}" } }
  }]
}
```

#### 6.1.3 Network Configuration

| Aspect | Value |
|---|---|
| VPC placement | Platform VPC, private application subnets (2 AZs) for ECS tasks; ALB in public subnets |
| Egress | NAT gateway for S3/MWAA AWS service endpoints; VPC endpoints preferred for S3 (Gateway) and SSM (Interface) |
| SG `laminar-dataoutbound-do-admin-api-sg-{env}` | Ingress: TCP 8000 from ALB SG only. Egress: TCP 5432 → `laminar-dataoutbound-cofig-db-sg-{env}`; TCP 443 → 0.0.0.0/0 (MWAA REST API, S3, SSM) |
| ALB SG | Ingress: TCP 443 from approved admin CIDR allowlist only |

#### 6.1.4 Security Controls & Encryption

- JWT bearer validation on all endpoints except `/health`; role check `export-admin` → 401/403 per SCRUM-479 AC#7.
- Credential fields encrypted with the shared KMS key before persistence; masked in all read responses.
- KMS key policy (shared `laminar-dataoutbound-{env}` key, deletion protection driven by `deletion_protection_enabled` per SCRUM-485 AC#3):

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Sid": "RootFullAccess", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::${account}:root" },
      "Action": "kms:*", "Resource": "*" },
    { "Sid": "ApiDecryptOnly", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::${account}:role/laminar-dataoutbound-do-admin-api-role-${env}" },
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"], "Resource": "*" }
  ]
}
```

#### 6.1.5 Observability & Alerting

| Metric | Namespace | Threshold | Alarm Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| HTTP 5xx count | AWS/ApplicationELB | ≥ 5 in 5 min | SNS → on-call |
| TargetResponseTime p99 | AWS/ApplicationELB | > 1 s for 10 min | SNS (500 ms guardrail breach trend) |
| Task running count | ECS/ContainerInsights | < 1 for 5 min | SNS |
| Auth failures (401/403 rate) | Laminar/DataOutbound (EMF) | > 50 in 5 min | SNS (security review) |

#### 6.1.6 Disaster Recovery & Backup

RTO 2 h / RPO 24 h inherited from `cofig_db` (the API itself is stateless; recovery = redeploy task definition). No independent backup mechanism; multi-AZ ALB + 2 tasks in staging/prod.

#### 6.1.7 Infrastructure Assumptions

- Q: Which identity provider issues the JWTs? A: The platform's existing OIDC issuer, configured via `apis/config.yml` (`auth_issuer` per environment). Justification: standard_api pattern requires JWT/OAuth2; issuer is externalized config.
- Q: Rate limiting? A: Token-bucket, 100 req/min per client IP at the ALB/WAF layer. Justification: standard_api security pattern default.
- Q: Is `rds-db:connect` needed for the API? A: No — Postgres credentials come from SSM SecureString over TLS (`sslmode=require`); IAM DB auth is not used. Justification: resolves review comment 7.1 (invalid `rds-db:connect` pairing removed).

### 6.2. Infrastructure Specification: scheduler
<a id="laminar-sec-g.6.imp_aws_aws_eventbridge_2"></a>

#### 6.2.1 Resource Configuration & Sizing
| Parameter | Value | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| Component Type | `aws_eventbridge` | Serverless event bus and rule scheduler. |
| Rule Name | `scheduler` | Exact resource name specified in architecture graph context. |
| Schedule Expression | Cron / Rate Expression (e.g., `@daily`) | Drives time-based batch export cadence triggers. |
| Target Type | MWAA REST API / Airflow Trigger | Invokes the `orchestrator` DAG on schedule. |

#### 6.2.2 IAM Role & Policies
IAM execution role allowing EventBridge to invoke the target MWAA environment:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "EventBridgeInvokeMwaaOrchestrator",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "airflow:PublishMetrics",
        "airflow:CreateCliToken"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:airflow:${var.aws_region}:${var.aws_account_id}:environment/orchestrator"
    }
  ]
}
```

Trust Policy:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "Service": "events.amazonaws.com"
      },
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### 6.2.3 Network Configuration
- **VPC Placement**: N/A (AWS native serverless control-plane service).
- **Subnet Tier**: N/A.

| Direction | Port | Protocol | Destination / Source | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Outbound | 443 | HTTPS | MWAA Control Plane API | Triggering export orchestration workflows |

#### 6.2.4 Security Controls & Encryption
- **Encryption in Transit**: TLS 1.3 enforced for all EventBridge rule target invocations.
- **Least Privilege**: Rule permissions are strictly scoped to invoke only the designated `orchestrator` MWAA environment.

#### 6.2.5 Observability & Alerting
| Metric | Namespace | Threshold | Alarm Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Invocations` | `AWS/Events` | N/A (Monitored for volume) | None |
| `FailedInvocations` | `AWS/Events` | `Sum >= 1 over 5 minutes` | Trigger SNS alert for scheduler delivery failures |

#### 6.2.6 Disaster Recovery & Backup
- **RPO / RTO**: RPO: 0 (Stateless rule definitions); RTO: Immediate (Provisioned via Terraform IaC).
- **Backup Mechanism**: Rule configurations are version-controlled in Git and provisioned via Terraform.

#### 6.2.7 Infrastructure Assumptions
- **Q**: How are schedule expressions managed across environments?
  - **A**: Managed via `values.yaml` environment overlay files.
  - **Justification**: Enables faster test cadences in `dev` and production-aligned cadences in `prod`.

#### 6.3.1 Resource Configuration & Sizing
| Parameter | Value | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| MWAA Environment Class | `mw1.small` | Sized adequately for scheduling and coordinating lightweight metadata orchestration tasks. |
| Environment Name | `orchestrator` | Matches user diagram specification. |
| Schedule Expression | `@daily` | Triggers orchestration workflow daily per user configuration. |
| Max Active Runs | 1 | Prevents overlapping workflow executions for the orchestrator DAG. |
| Catchup | `false` | Disables historical backfilling for scheduled runs. |

#### 6.3.2 IAM Role & Policies
**MWAA Execution Role Trust Policy:**
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "Service": "airflow.amazonaws.com"
      },
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}
```

**MWAA Execution IAM Policy (`laminar-mwaa-orchestrator-role-${env}`):**
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "airflow:PublishMetrics"
      ],

    },

      ]

      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "rds-db:connect"
      ],

      "Effect": "Allow",

        "kms:GenerateDataKey"
```

#### 6.3.3 Network Configuration
- **VPC Placement**: Private MWAA Subnets (isolated subnets with VPC endpoints for S3, CloudWatch, and RDS).
- **Subnet Tier**: Private isolation tier with strict NACL boundaries.
- **Security Group Rules**:
| Direction | Protocol | Port Range | Source / Destination | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inbound | TCP | 443 | VPC Internal / ALB SG | Access to Airflow Webserver UI / API |
| Outbound | TCP | 5432 | `cofig_db` SG | Query active export configurations in RDS |
| Outbound | TCP | 443 | S3, SSM, CloudWatch Endpoints | DAG artifact loading and log emission |

#### 6.3.4 Security Controls & Encryption
- **Encryption at Rest**: S3 DAG bucket encrypted with SSE-S3 (`AES256`); RDS metadata encrypted via KMS CMK.
- **Transport Encryption**: HTTPS (TLS 1.3) enforced for all MWAA REST API interactions and web UI access.

#### 6.3.5 Observability & Alerting
| Metric | Namespace | Threshold | Alarm Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| DAGTaskFailures | AmazonMWAA | >= 1 failure over 15 minutes | SNS notification to platform operators |
| WorkerCpuUtilization | AmazonMWAA | > 85% for 15 minutes | CloudWatch warning alarm |

#### 6.3.6 Disaster Recovery & Backup
- **RTO (Recovery Time Objective)**: 4 hours (MWAA environment snapshot restoration).
- **RPO (Recovery Point Objective)**: 24 hours (Airflow metadata database daily automated snapshot).
- **Backup Mechanism**: Automated RDS PostgreSQL snapshots backing the MWAA metadata store.

#### 6.3.7 Infrastructure Assumptions
- Q: How does the orchestrator trigger child DAGs?
  A: Via the Airflow REST API (`TriggerDagRunOperator`) passing configuration payloads containing the lineage UUID.
  Justification: Standard decoupled parent-child execution pattern in Apache Airflow.
- Q: Where is DAG code stored?
  A: In an S3 bucket dedicated to MWAA DAG storage (`laminar-mwaa-dags-${env}`).
  Justification: Standard MWAA deployment requirement.

### 6.6. Infrastructure Specification: dev
<a id="laminar-sec-g.6.imp_aws_aws_redshift_6"></a>

<!-- laminar:diagram-settings:imp-aws-aws_redshift-6 -->
**Diagram settings (user decisions — authoritative)**

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `node_type` | `dc2.large` |
| `number_of_nodes` | `2` |
| `database_name` | `dev` |
| `cluster_identifier` | `golden_data_source` |

<!-- /laminar:diagram-settings -->

#### 6.6.1 Resource Configuration & Sizing

| Parameter | Value | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| node_type | `dc2.large` | User-set (authoritative) |
| number_of_nodes | `2` | User-set (authoritative) |
| database_name | `dev` | User-set (authoritative) |
| cluster_identifier | `golden_data_source` | User-set (authoritative) |
| Terraform resource | `golden_entity_source_store_redshift` (in `terraform/redshift.tf`) — **externally owned; referenced, not provisioned** | SCRUM-485: excluded from allowlist check; this section documents our consumption contract only |

#### 6.6.2 IAM Role & Policies

The pipeline does not manage this cluster's IAM. Our side of the contract: the EMR job execution role (`laminar-dataoutbound-emr-job-role-{env}`) authenticates to `golden_data_source` using a **read-only database user** provisioned in the cluster by its owner, with credentials resolved from SSM SecureString at `/laminar/dataoutbound/{env}/emr-do/redshift/`. No cross-account Redshift API actions (`redshift:GetClusterCredentials` etc.) are granted; access is purely JDBC over TLS with a static read-only user. If the cluster owner later requires IAM-based auth, the role would need `redshift:GetClusterCredentials` scoped to `dbuser:golden_data_source/readonly_user` — raised as a recommendation only.

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Sid": "ReadRedshiftCredentials", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["ssm:GetParameter"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ssm:${region}:${account}:parameter/laminar/dataoutbound/${env}/emr-do/redshift/*" }
  ]
}
```

Trust policy: standard EMR Serverless service principal (`emr-serverless.amazonaws.com`) with `aws:SourceAccount` condition.

#### 6.6.3 Network Configuration

| Aspect | Value |
|---|---|
| Placement | Externally owned cluster in private database subnets of the platform VPC (assumed co-located with pipeline) |
| Path | `emr_do` Spark job → JDBC (port 5439) over TLS from EMR Serverless private-subnet worker SG |
| SG rule (our side) | `laminar-dataoutbound-emr-job-sg-{env}` egress TCP 5439 → Redshift cluster SG; cluster SG ingress restricted to that SG |

#### 6.6.4 Security Controls & Encryption

- TLS enforced on JDBC connections (`sslmode=require`); read-only DB user only; KMS encryption at rest is the cluster owner's responsibility (assumed enabled).

#### 6.6.5 Observability & Alerting

| Metric | Namespace | Threshold | Alarm Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPUUtilization | AWS/Redshift | > 90% for 15 min during extraction windows | SNS (owner notified; we consume) |
| WLMQueueWaitTime (our query queue) | AWS/Redshift | > 300 s | SNS → pipeline on-call |

#### 6.6.6 Disaster Recovery & Backup

N/A for this specification — the cluster is externally owned; its backup/RPO is the owner's responsibility. Our recovery posture: extraction jobs are idempotent and re-runnable against the source at any time (RTO = job re-run, RPO = none, source of truth is the cluster).

#### 6.6.7 Infrastructure Assumptions

- Q: Is the cluster in the same account/VPC as the pipeline? A: Assumed yes (same account, platform VPC, private subnets). Justification: no cross-account trust is provisioned; resolves review comment 7.1 (EMR role targets the cluster via a read-only DB user, not cross-account credentials).
- Q: Naming — `golden_data_source` vs `golden_entity_source_store_redshift`? A: `golden_data_source` is the physical cluster identifier (user-set); `golden_entity_source_store_redshift` is the Terraform resource name referencing it. Both are used consistently in their respective layers.

#### 6.7.7 Infrastructure Assumptions

- Q: How are credentials managed?
  A: Master credentials generated via Terraform and stored encrypted in SSM Parameter Store (SecureString).
  Justification: Prevents hardcoded database passwords in infrastructure code.

### 6.8. Infrastructure Specification: staging_bucet_internal
<a id="laminar-sec-g.6.imp_aws_aws_s3_bucket_8"></a>

<!-- laminar:diagram-settings:imp-aws-aws_s3_bucket-8 -->
**Diagram settings (user decisions — authoritative)**

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `versioning` | `false` |
| `encryption` | `AES256` |
| `public_access_block` | `true` |
| `lifecycle_enabled` | `false` |

| `lifecycle_glacier_days` | `90` |
| `bucket_name` | `staging_bucet_internal` |

<!-- /laminar:diagram-settings -->

#### 6.8.1 Resource Configuration & Sizing
| Parameter | Value | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| Bucket Name | `staging_bucet_internal` | User-defined authoritative physical resource name for internal staging objects. |
| Versioning | `False` | User decision; transient staging files do not require version history. |
| Encryption | `AES256` (SSE-S3) | Mandatory server-side encryption at rest for all staged payloads. |
| Public Access Block | `True` | Strict security control blocking all public bucket policies and ACLs. |
| Lifecycle Enabled | `False` | User decision; static lifecycle disabled on bucket resource (Recommendation: enable 7-day lifecycle rule per SCRUM-486 operational requirements). |
| Lifecycle Transition Days | `30` | User decision; standard transition threshold for non-active objects. |
| Lifecycle Glacier Days | `90` | User decision; archive threshold for retained staging records. |

#### 6.8.2 IAM Role & Policies
The S3 bucket policy and associated IAM resource policies enforce least-privilege access for `emr_do` (writing staged export files), `egress-lambda` (triggering on object creation), and `egress dag` (reading staged files).

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "EnforceTLSRequestsOnly",
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:*",
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::staging_bucet_internal",
        "arn:aws:s3:::staging_bucet_internal/*"
      ],
      "Condition": {
        "Bool": {
          "aws:SecureTransport": "false"
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowEMRAndMWAAccess",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "AWS": [
          "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/laminar-emr-execution-role-prod",
          "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/laminar-mwaa-execution-role-prod"
        ]
      },
      "Action": [
        "s3:PutObject",
        "s3:GetObject",
        "s3:ListBucket",
        "s3:DeleteObject"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::staging_bucet_internal",
        "arn:aws:s3:::staging_bucet_internal/*"
      ]
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowLambdaInvocationTrigger",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "Service": "s3.amazonaws.com"
      },
      "Action": "s3:PutObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::staging_bucet_internal/*"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### 6.8.3 Network Configuration
- **VPC Placement**: Regional S3 service accessed via Amazon S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint attached to private subnets.
- **Subnet Tier**: Private application and data subnets (no direct internet route).
- **Security Group Rules**: S3 communicates via AWS backbone; internal VPC route tables enforce VPC endpoint routing.

#### 6.8.4 Security Controls & Encryption
- **Encryption at Rest**: AES-256 (SSE-S3) enforced on all put operations.
- **Encryption in Transit**: TLS 1.3 enforced via bucket policy condition `aws:SecureTransport = true`.
- **Access Control**: Public Access Block fully enabled (`block_public_acls = true`, `block_public_policy = true`, `ignore_public_acls = true`, `restrict_public_buckets = true`).

#### 6.8.5 Observability & Alerting
| Metric | Namespace | Threshold | Alarm Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `5xxErrors` | `AWS/S3` | Sum >= 1 over 5 minutes | SNS Topic -> Operations Alert |
| `BucketSizeBytes` | `AWS/S3` | Sum >= 50 GB over 24 hours | SNS Topic -> Capacity Warning |
| `NumberOfObjects` | `AWS/S3` | Sum >= 100,000 over 1 hour | SNS Topic -> Accumulation Alert |

#### 6.8.6 Disaster Recovery & Backup
- **RPO / RTO**: RPO = 0 (stateless transient staging); RTO < 1 hour (re-runnable via child export DAG).
- **Backup Mechanism**: Transient staging files are regenerated by upstream EMR jobs; versioning is disabled per user specification.

#### 6.8.7 Infrastructure Assumptions
- **Q**: Why is `lifecycle_enabled` set to `False` in the diagram settings while user stories mandate a 7-day retention?
  **A**: The diagram setting (`lifecycle_enabled = false`) is authoritative for provisioning, but operational requirements mandate lifecycle cleanup.
  **Justification**: Provisioned infrastructure respects the authoritative user decision, while recommending an explicit lifecycle rule overlay via external config management or terraform update in subsequent iterations.

| runtime | `python3.11` | User-set (authoritative) |
| handler | `lambda_function.lambda_handler` | User-set (authoritative) |
| memory_mb | `512` | User-set (authoritative) |
| timeout_seconds | `30` | User-set (authoritative) |
| vpc_enabled | `false` | User-set (authoritative) |
| environment_variables | `{}` (none beyond defaults; secrets via SSM at runtime) | User-set (authoritative) |
| Terraform resource | `egress_lambda` (in `terraform/lambda.tf`) | Blueprint |
| Trigger | S3 event notification on `staging_bucet_internal` (`s3:ObjectCreated:*`, filter prefix `exports/`), SQS on-failure destination `laminar-dataoutbound-egress-lambda-dlq-{env}` | Frozen contract; DLQ per best practice |
| Reserved concurrency | 50 | Bounds MWAA trigger fan-out under bulk staging writes |

#### 6.9.2 IAM Role & Policies

Execution role `laminar-dataoutbound-egress-lambda-role-{env}`. MWAA DAG triggering uses the correct REST-invocation actions (`airflow:CreateApiToken` / `airflow:InvokeRestApi`), not the invalid `airflow:CreateDagRun`:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Sid": "ReadEventMetadata", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::staging_bucet_internal/exports/*" },
    { "Sid": "TriggerEgressDagViaMwaaRestApi", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["airflow:CreateApiToken", "airflow:InvokeRestApi"],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:airflow:${region}:${account}:environment/laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-${env}",
        "arn:aws:airflow:${region}:${account}:environment/laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-${env}#dags/egress dag" ] },
    { "Sid": "ReadSsmSecrets", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["ssm:GetParameter"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ssm:${region}:${account}:parameter/laminar/dataoutbound/${env}/egress-lambda/*" },
    { "Sid": "KmsDecrypt", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:${region}:${account}:key/${laminar_dataoutbound_key_id}" },
    { "Sid": "WriteLogs", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["logs:CreateLogStream", "logs:PutLogEvents"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:logs:${region}:${account}:log-group:/laminar/dataoutbound/egress-lambda/${env}:*" }
  ]
}
```

Trust policy:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": { "Service": "lambda.amazonaws.com" },
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
    "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:SourceAccount": "${account}" } }
  }]
}
```

#### 6.9.3 Network Configuration

| Aspect | Value |
|---|---|
| Placement | No VPC (user decision `vpc_enabled = false`); reaches S3, MWAA REST API and SSM over AWS public service endpoints via IAM auth |
| SG rules | N/A — no ENI is provisioned |

#### 6.9.4 Security Controls & Encryption

- All AWS API calls over TLS; SSM SecureString parameters decrypted with the shared KMS key; no secrets in environment variables (user set `environment_variables = {}`).
- Idempotency: object-key tracking (DynamoDB-free — dedup via deterministic DAG run key `lineage_uuid` from the object key) ensures exactly one `egress dag` run per staged file (SCRUM-482 AC#3).

#### 6.9.5 Observability & Alerting

| Metric | Namespace | Threshold | Alarm Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Errors | AWS/Lambda | ≥ 1 in 5 min | SNS → on-call |
| Throttles | AWS/Lambda | ≥ 1 in 5 min | SNS |
| Duration p99 | AWS/Lambda | > 25 s (approaching 30 s timeout) | SNS |
| DLQ message count | AWS/SQS (DLQ) | ≥ 1 | SNS (failed trigger = silent egress gap) |

#### 6.9.6 Disaster Recovery & Backup

Stateless; RTO = redeploy (minutes), RPO = 0 (no state). Failed invocations land in the DLQ and are replayed manually; the S3 source object remains in `staging_bucet_internal` for 7 days, so a missed trigger is recoverable by re-invoking with the same object key.

#### 6.9.7 Infrastructure Assumptions

- Q: How does the Lambda reach MWAA without a VPC? A: Via the MWAA REST API over HTTPS with `airflow:CreateApiToken`/`InvokeRestApi`; MWAA public REST endpoints are used (MWAA web access via VPC does not affect the REST API path). Justification: consistent with `vpc_enabled = false` user decision.
- Q: DLQ retention? A: 14 days on `laminar-dataoutbound-egress-lambda-dlq-{env}`. Justification: mainstream default, allows replay within the 7-day staging window.

#### 6.10.3 Network Configuration
- **VPC Placement**: MWAA private worker subnets across Multi-AZ.
- **Subnet Tier**: Private Subnets with NAT Gateway egress.

| Direction | Port | Protocol | Source / Destination CIDR | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Outbound | 443 | HTTPS | `0.0.0.0/0` (via NAT Gateway) | Push exports to Azure Blob, GCS, and AWS S3 destinations |
| Outbound | 22 | SSH | External SFTP Server IP / CIDR | Push encrypted exports to customer SFTP server |

#### 6.10.4 Security Controls & Encryption
- **Fail-Closed PGP**: If PGP encryption fails or keys are invalid, execution aborts immediately, zero unencrypted bytes are transmitted, and a `TRANSFER_FAILED` audit event is emitted.
- **Transport Security**: TLS 1.3 for S3, HTTPS for Azure and GCS, and SSH with strict host-key verification for SFTP.

#### 6.10.5 Observability & Alerting
| Metric | Namespace | Threshold | Alarm Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DAGExecutionFailed` | `AWS/MWAA` | Sum >= 1 over 1 execution | SNS Topic -> PagerDuty Operations |
| `TaskDuration` | `AWS/MWAA` | > 7200 seconds | CloudWatch warning alarm |

#### 6.10.6 Disaster Recovery & Backup
- **RTO / RPO**: RTO < 4 hours, RPO = 0.
- **Backup Mechanism**: DAG code version-controlled in Git and deployed to MWAA DAGs S3 bucket; state managed in MWAA metadata database.

#### 6.10.7 Infrastructure Assumptions
- **Q:** How are PGP public keys managed per customer?
  **A:** Stored securely as `SecureString` parameters in AWS SSM Parameter Store keyed by `customer_id`.
  **Justification:** Centralizes secret rotation and avoids hardcoding cryptographic keys in configuration code.

### 6.11. Infrastructure Specification: Customer Azure Blob Destination
<a id="laminar-sec-g.6.imp_azure_blob_store_13"></a>
#### 6.11.1 Resource Configuration & Sizing
| Parameter | Value | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| Component Type | `blob_store` (External / Third-Party) | Customer-owned storage endpoint; outside our Terraform provisioning scope per architecture blueprint. |
| Protocol / Integration | HTTPS (REST API) | Secure, encrypted transport for data egress pushing packaged export files. |
| Connection Method | Connection String / SAS Token via SSM SecureString | Credentials are externalized securely and retrieved at runtime by the egress workflow. |
| Max Transfer Payload | 1 GB per file | Aligns with the 1 GB per-customer file export limit defined in the system specification. |
| Retry Policy | 3 attempts with exponential backoff | Ensures transient network or throttling errors do not cause immediate pipeline failure. |

#### 6.11.2 IAM Role & Policies
As `Customer Azure Blob Destination` is an external third-party component, no AWS IAM roles are provisioned for its internal architecture. However, the internal pipeline component (`egress dag` / execution role) requires permission to access the corresponding connection secrets stored in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Below is the IAM policy for the pipeline execution role to retrieve the target Azure credentials:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "ReadAzureDestinationSecrets",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "ssm:GetParameter",
        "ssm:GetParameters"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ssm:${var.aws_region}:${var.aws_account_id}:parameter/laminar/egress/azure/*"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### 6.11.3 Network Configuration
- **VPC Placement**: N/A (External third-party endpoint; accessed via public/hybrid cloud HTTPS routing).
- **Subnet Tier**: N/A (Egress requests originate from private subnets hosting MWAA worker nodes via NAT Gateway).

| Direction | Port | Protocol | Destination / Source | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Outbound | 443 | HTTPS | Customer Azure Blob REST API Endpoint | Pushing encrypted export packages and manifest control files |

#### 6.11.4 Security Controls & Encryption
- **Transport Security**: Enforces HTTPS with TLS 1.3 / 1.2 for all upload requests.
- **Data Protection**: Payloads are pre-encrypted with fail-closed PGP before transmission.
- **Credential Storage**: Storage account connection strings or SAS tokens are stored as encrypted `SecureString` values in AWS SSM Parameter Store using KMS CMK encryption.

#### 6.11.5 Observability & Alerting
| Metric | Namespace | Threshold | Alarm Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TransferFailedCount` | `Laminar/DataOutbound/Egress` | `Sum >= 1 over 5 minutes` | Trigger SNS alert and log `TRANSFER_FAILED` audit event |
| `TransferDuration` | `Laminar/DataOutbound/Egress` | `> 3600 seconds` | Trigger SNS warning alert |

#### 6.11.6 Disaster Recovery & Backup
- **RPO / RTO**: RPO: N/A (Stateless egress push); RTO: 4 hours (recovery governed by pipeline retry limits and manual operational review).
- **Backup Mechanism**: Customer-owned destination; our pipeline maintains execution idempotency and stores execution audit logs in `audit_bucket` to support safe re-runs upon delivery failure.

#### 6.11.7 Infrastructure Assumptions
- **Q**: How are Azure storage credentials provisioned?
  - **A**: Provided out-of-band by the customer and stored securely by Acme administrators in SSM Parameter Store.
  - **Justification**: Protects sensitive secrets while allowing automated retrieval by the egress pipeline.
- **Q**: What happens if the Azure endpoint is unreachable after retries?
  - **A**: The transfer task marks the execution as failed, emits a `TRANSFER_FAILED` audit event, and halts further delivery until resolved.
  - **Justification**: Enforces fail-closed data governance and triggers operational review.

### 6.13. Infrastructure Specification: audit_bucket
<a id="laminar-sec-g.6.imp_aws_aws_s3_bucket_15"></a>

<!-- laminar:diagram-settings:imp-aws-aws_s3_bucket-15 -->
**Diagram settings (user decisions — authoritative)**

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `versioning` | `false` |
| `encryption` | `AES256` |
| `public_access_block` | `true` |
| `lifecycle_enabled` | `true` |
| `lifecycle_transition_days` | `30` |
| `lifecycle_glacier_days` | `90` |
| `bucket_name` | `audit_bucket` |

<!-- /laminar:diagram-settings -->

#### 6.13.1 Resource Configuration & Sizing

| Parameter | Value | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| bucket_name | `audit_bucket` | User-set (authoritative) |
| Terraform resource | `audit_execution_log_store_s3` (in `terraform/s3.tf`) | Blueprint |
| versioning | `false` | User-set (authoritative) |
| encryption | `AES256` (SSE-S3) | User-set (authoritative) |
| public_access_block | `true` (all four settings) | User-set (authoritative) |
| lifecycle_enabled | `true`; transition to STANDARD_IA at 30 d, GLACIER at 90 d | User-set (authoritative) |
| Key layout | `admin/`, `spark/`, `egress/` prefixes; hash-prefixed object keys (`{sha1(event_id)[:2]}/{date}/{event_id}.json`) | Distributes PUT load across S3 partitions |
| Deletion protection | `prevent_destroy` guarded by `deletion_protection_enabled` variable (false in dev, true in staging/prod) | SCRUM-485 AC#3–AC#5 |

#### 6.13.2 IAM Role & Policies

Bucket policy — writers are exactly the three pipeline roles (single MWAA execution role `laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-execution-role-{env}` serves all three DAGs, plus the EMR job role and API task role; no per-DAG roles exist):

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Sid": "DenyNonTls", "Effect": "Deny", "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:*", "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket",
        "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket/*" ],
      "Condition": { "Bool": { "aws:SecureTransport": "false" } } },
    { "Sid": "ApiWritesAdminEvents", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::${account}:role/laminar-dataoutbound-do-admin-api-role-${env}" },
      "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket/admin/*" },
    { "Sid": "EmrWritesSparkEvents", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::${account}:role/laminar-dataoutbound-emr-job-role-${env}" },
      "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket/spark/*" },
    { "Sid": "MwaaWritesEgressEvents", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::${account}:role/laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-execution-role-${env}" },
      "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket/egress/*" },
    { "Sid": "DenyUnlistedWrites", "Effect": "Deny", "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket/*",
      "Condition": { "StringNotEquals": { "aws:PrincipalArn": [
        "arn:aws:iam::${account}:role/laminar-dataoutbound-do-admin-api-role-${env}",
        "arn:aws:iam::${account}:role/laminar-dataoutbound-emr-job-role-${env}",
        "arn:aws:iam::${account}:role/laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-execution-role-${env}" ] } } }
  ]
}
```

Note on immutability: with `versioning = false` (user decision), S3 cannot enforce true write-once semantics via bucket policy alone; the DenyUnlistedWrites statement restricts *who* may write, not *what* may be overwritten. **Recommendation:** enable Object Lock (governance mode, 90-day retention) — this requires versioning, so it conflicts with the user's `versioning = false` and is raised here only as a recommendation, not applied.

#### 6.13.3 Network Configuration

| Aspect | Value |
|---|---|
| Placement | Regional S3 bucket, no VPC attachment; accessed via S3 Gateway VPC endpoint from MWAA/EMR/ECS private subnets |
| SG rules | N/A — S3 is not VPC-resident; access controlled by bucket policy + VPC endpoint policy restricting to `audit_bucket` |

#### 6.13.4 Security Controls & Encryption

- SSE-S3 (AES256) per user decision; TLS enforced via DenyNonTls statement.
- No public access (all four Block Public Access settings true).

#### 6.13.5 Observability & Alerting

| Metric | Namespace | Threshold | Alarm Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| BucketRequestsErrors (4xx/5xx) | AWS/S3 | ≥ 10 in 5 min | SNS → on-call |
| BucketSizeBytes | AWS/S3 | > 50 GB | SNS (cost anomaly) |
| Audit write gap (custom EMF: last audit event age) | Laminar/DataOutbound | > 15 min without any event during an active run | SNS (silent-audit-failure guardrail) |

#### 6.13.6 Disaster Recovery & Backup

RPO 24 h / RTO 2 h (platform standard). Mechanism: S3 cross-AZ durability (11 nines) plus lifecycle tiering; **no Cross-Region Replication** — CRR requires versioning, which the user set to `false`, and CRR would be asynchronous in any case. Recovery relies on S3 durability; if cross-region audit resilience is required, revisit the versioning decision.

#### 6.13.7 Infrastructure Assumptions

- Q: Is audit immutability (WORM) required? A: Not enforced in this configuration because `versioning = false` precludes Object Lock; write access is restricted to the three pipeline roles. Justification: resolves review comment 6.13.2 without contradicting the user decision.
- Q: Retention beyond the 30 d/90 d lifecycle? A: Glacier objects retained indefinitely until a retention policy is confirmed. Justification: lifecycle values are user-set; final retention pending logging-standard confirmation (SCRUM-486).

### 6.14. Infrastructure Specification: customer SFTP server
<a id="laminar-sec-g.6.imp_standard_standard_sftp_11"></a>

<!-- laminar:diagram-settings:imp-standard-standard_sftp-11 -->
**Diagram settings (user decisions — authoritative)**

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `port` | `22` |
| `authentication_method` | `SSH Key` |
| `server_name` | `customer SFTP server` |

<!-- /laminar:diagram-settings -->

#### 6.14.1 Network Configuration
- **Network Path**: Outbound SFTP over SSH (port 22) from `egress dag` workers via private subnet NAT Gateway to customer SFTP server IP / hostname.
- **Egress Security Group Rules**: Outbound TCP port 22 allowed to customer SFTP server CIDR.
- **Customer Allowlist Requirements**: Customer must allow-list Acme's static NAT Gateway elastic IPs on their SFTP firewall.

#### 6.14.2 Security Controls & Encryption
- **Authentication**: SSH Key-based authentication (private key retrieved from SSM Parameter Store SecureString).
- **Host Key Verification**: Strict host-key verification enabled (connection refused and zero bytes sent if host key changes or fails verification).
- **Data Encryption**: PGP encryption applied to export payloads before SFTP transmission; transit encrypted via SSH/TLS transport layer.

#### 6.14.3 Observability & Alerting
| Metric / Check | Threshold | Alarm Action |
|---|---|---|
| SFTP Connection Failures | >= 3 consecutive failures | SNS Topic -> SFTP Delivery Alert |
| Host Key Mismatch | Immediate failure (0 retries) | SNS Topic -> Security Incident Alert |

#### 6.14.4 Infrastructure Assumptions
- **Q**: What happens if host-key verification fails?
  **A**: Connection is immediately refused, zero bytes are transmitted, no retry is attempted, an alert is raised, and a `TRANSFER_FAILED` event is written to the audit store.
  **Justification**: Enforces strict security compliance and prevents man-in-the-middle attacks.

## 7. Security, Identity & Secrets Management
<a id="laminar-sec-g.7"></a>
### 7.1 Cross-Service IAM Architecture

One IAM role per compute component, all least-privilege with explicit ARNs (no wildcard accounts or resource wildcards). Role names follow the convention in §g.3 (`laminar-dataoutbound-{component}-role-{env}`). The three MWAA DAGs share the single MWAA execution role `laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-execution-role-{env}` (MWAA environments have one execution role; DAG-level separation is enforced via Airflow connections and per-job IAM, not per-DAG roles).

**Trust policy (common pattern)** — each service principal assumes its own role:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": { "Service": "ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com" },
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
    "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:SourceAccount": "${account_id}" } }
  }]
}
```
(`Service` varies: `ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com` for do-admin-api, `lambda.amazonaws.com` for egress-lambda, `airflow.amazonaws.com` + `ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com` for MWAA, `emr-serverless.amazonaws.com` for the EMR job role, `events.amazonaws.com` for the scheduler invoke role.)

**do-admin-api task role** (`laminar-dataoutbound-do-admin-api-role-{env}`) — corrected per review: no `rds-db:connect` (the API uses a stored DB credential, not IAM DB auth), no `ssm:PutParameter` (read-only SSM), and the correct MWAA REST action:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "ReadConfigDbCredential",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["ssm:GetParameter", "ssm:GetParameters"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ssm:${region}:${account}:parameter/laminar/dataoutbound/${env}/do-admin-api/*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "TriggerOrchestratorViaMwaaRestApi",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["airflow:InvokeRestApi", "airflow:CreateWebLoginToken"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:airflow:${region}:${account}:environment/laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-${env}",
      "Condition": { "StringLike": { "airflow:endpoint": "*/dags/*/dagRuns" } }
    },
    {
      "Sid": "WriteAdminAuditEvents",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:PutObject"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket/admin/*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "KmsDecryptSsmSecureStrings",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:${region}:${account}:key/${kms_key_id}"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Egress Lambda execution role** (`laminar-dataoutbound-egress-lambda-role-{env}`) — corrected MWAA action:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "ReadStagingEventMetadata",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::staging_bucet_internal/*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "TriggerEgressDagViaMwaaRestApi",

      "Condition": { "StringLike": { "airflow:endpoint": "*/dags/*/dagRuns" } }
    },
    {
      "Sid": "KmsDecryptSsmSecureStrings",

    }

}
```
Lambda async-invocation DLQ: `laminar-dataoutbound-egress-lambda-dlq-{env}` (SQS), configured as the function's `DeadLetterConfig`.

**MWAA execution role** (`laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-execution-role-{env}`) — used by all three DAGs (orchestrator, child_export_dag, egress dag):

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Sid": "ReadConfigDbCreds", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["ssm:GetParameter", "ssm:GetParameters"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ssm:${region}:${account}:parameter/laminar/dataoutbound/${env}/*" },
    { "Sid": "SubmitEmrJobs", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["emr-serverless:StartJobRun", "emr-serverless:GetJobRun", "emr-serverless:CancelJobRun"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:emr-serverless:${region}:${account}:applications/${emr_app_id}",
                   "arn:aws:emr-serverless:${region}:${account}:applications/${emr_app_id}/jobruns/*"] },
    { "Sid": "ReadStagingWriteAudit", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject", "s3:ListBucket"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::staging_bucet_internal", "arn:aws:s3:::staging_bucet_internal/*",
                   "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket", "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket/egress/*"] },
    { "Sid": "KmsDecrypt", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:${region}:${account}:key/${kms_key_id}" }
  ]
}
```

Cross-account delivery to the customer bucket (customer-owned, `is_external = true`) is performed by the egress dag assuming a customer-provided role — pinned, not wildcarded:

```json
{
  "Sid": "AssumeCustomerEgressRole",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:iam::${customer_account_id}:role/CustomerCrossAccountEgressRole",
  "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "sts:ExternalId": "${customer_external_id}" } }
}
```
`${customer_account_id}` and `${customer_external_id}` are per-connection values from `values.yaml` / SSM — never `*`.

**EMR Serverless job execution role** (`laminar-dataoutbound-emr-job-role-{env}`): reads the externally owned Redshift cluster `golden_data_source` (database `dev`) via JDBC credentials resolved from SSM — not via cluster-level IAM actions, because the Golden Entity Source Store is externally owned and we hold no IAM control over it. The role therefore grants only S3 staging/audit writes and KMS decrypt; Redshift access is credential-based (read-only user) over TLS. No cross-account Redshift trust is required.

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Sid": "WriteStaging", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:PutObject", "s3:GetObject", "s3:AbortMultipartUpload", "s3:ListMultipartUploadParts"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::staging_bucet_internal/exports/*" },
    { "Sid": "WriteSparkAudit", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:PutObject"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::audit_bucket/spark/*" },
    { "Sid": "KmsDecrypt", "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:${region}:${account}:key/${kms_key_id}" }
  ]
}
```

**Scheduler invoke role** (`laminar-dataoutbound-scheduler-role-{env}`): `airflow:InvokeRestApi` + `airflow:CreateWebLoginToken` on `arn:aws:airflow:${region}:${account}:environment/laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-${env}` only, with the same `airflow:endpoint` condition; failed deliveries route to `laminar-dataoutbound-scheduler-dlq-{env}` after EventBridge retries (24 h max age).

**Bucket policies**: `staging_bucet_internal` allows `s3:GetObject`/`s3:PutObject` only to the EMR job role, MWAA execution role, and egress-lambda role ARNs; `audit_bucket` allows `s3:PutObject` only to the do-admin-api role (`admin/*`), EMR job role (`spark/*`), and MWAA execution role (`egress/*`). Both deny non-TLS (`aws:SecureTransport = false`) and enforce `aws:PublicAccessBlock` via the account-level block.

### 7.2 KMS CMK Strategy & Deletion Protection

One customer-managed key per environment: `laminar-dataoutbound-{env}` (alias `alias/laminar-dataoutbound-{env}`), used for SSM SecureString decryption and RDS storage encryption. Key policy grants `kms:Decrypt` only to the four workload roles above and `kms:GenerateDataKey` to RDS; admin operations restricted to the platform-engineer principal.

Per SCRUM-485 AC#3–AC#5, deletion protection is **never hardcoded**: a single per-environment variable `deletion_protection_enabled` in `values.yaml` drives every stateful resource:

| values.yaml key | dev | staging | prod | Applied to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deletion_protection_enabled` | `false` | `true` | `true` | `export_config_store_rds` (`deletion_protection`), `customer_staging_buckets_s3` + `audit_execution_log_store_s3` (Terraform `prevent_destroy` lifecycle block, conditionally created), KMS key (`prevent_destroy`) |

Effect: dev teardown (`terraform destroy`) exits 0; staging/prod teardown exits non-zero with no stateful resource destroyed.

### 7.3 Secrets & Parameter Store Patterns

| Secret | SSM path (SecureString, KMS `laminar-dataoutbound-{env}`) | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| cofig_db connection string | `/laminar/dataoutbound/{env}/do-admin-api/db-conn` | do-admin-api |
| cofig_db read-only creds (DAGs) | `/laminar/dataoutbound/{env}/mwaa/db-readonly` | orchestrator, child_export_dag |
| Redshift read-only creds | `/laminar/dataoutbound/{env}/emr/redshift-readonly` | emr_do (Spark JDBC) |
| PGP private keys per connection | `/laminar/dataoutbound/{env}/egress/pgp/{config_id}` | egress dag |
| Azure Entra ID service principal | `/laminar/dataoutbound/{env}/egress/azure/{config_id}` | egress dag |
| GCS service-account key | `/laminar/dataoutbound/{env}/egress/gcs/{config_id}` | egress dag |
| SFTP private key + host key | `/laminar/dataoutbound/{env}/egress/sftp/{config_id}` | egress dag |

All consumers resolve at runtime via `SsmClient` with decryption and short-lived caching; no secret is ever written to Terraform state, logs, or DAG code. Credential fields in `cofig_db` are additionally encrypted at the application layer before persistence (SCRUM-479 AC#1) and masked in all API responses.

### 7.4 Audit Logging

All audit events are CloudEvents-shaped JSON records written to `audit_bucket` under prefix `admin/`, `spark/`, or `egress/`, keyed by unique event ID (idempotent writes). Schema per SCRUM-486: `actor_id`, `timestamp_utc` (ISO-8601 ms, Z), `event_type` (enumerated set), `execution_id` (lineage UUID). Because `audit_bucket` has `versioning = false` (user decision), immutability is **not** claimed via S3 semantics; tamper-resistance is achieved through write-only IAM (no `s3:DeleteObject`, no `s3:GetObject` for writers) plus lifecycle tiering (30 d standard → Glacier at 90 d). Recommendation: if regulatory immutability is later required, enable Object Lock in compliance mode — this requires versioning and would need an explicit change to the user's `versioning = false` decision.

## 8. Observability, Monitoring & Alerting
<a id="laminar-sec-g.8"></a>
### 8.1 Centralised Log Aggregation & Log Group Configuration
Every pipeline component emits structured JSON logs containing correlation IDs and lineage UUIDs to explicitly provisioned CloudWatch Log Groups. In compliance with enterprise security standards, log retention is strictly set across all components.
- **Log Group Naming Convention**: `/aws/<service>/<component>-${var.environment}`
- **Retention Period**: `365` days (confirming the organization logging-standard value).
- **Log Groups Provisioned**:
  - `/aws/lambda/egress-lambda-${var.environment}`
  - `/aws/mwaa/orchestrator-${var.environment}`
  - `/aws/mwaa/child_export_dag-${var.environment}`
  - `/aws/mwaa/egress-dag-${var.environment}`
  - `/aws/emr-serverless/emr_do-${var.environment}`
  - `/aws/rds/cofig_db-${var.environment}`

### 8.2 OpenTelemetry & Audit Telemetry Pipeline
Structured CloudEvents-shaped audit records are published by every component directly to the `audit_bucket` and piped into the operational logging stream. Required event fields include `actor_id`, `timestamp_utc` (ISO-8601 with millisecond precision and Z suffix), `event_type` (`ADMIN_CREATE`, `ADMIN_UPDATE`, `ADMIN_DELETE`, `ADMIN_MANUAL_TRIGGER`, `EXECUTION_STARTED`, `EXECUTION_COMPLETED`, `TRANSFER_STARTED`, `TRANSFER_COMPLETED`, `TRANSFER_FAILED`), and `execution_id` (lineage UUID).

### 8.3 CloudWatch Alarms & SNS Notification Topics
Operational alerts are routed through a central Amazon SNS topic (`laminar-dataoutbound-alerts-${var.environment}`) configured with email and PagerDuty endpoints.
- **Key Alarm Thresholds**:
  - **Lambda Errors**: `Errors > 0` over a 1-minute evaluation period for `egress-lambda`.
  - **Lambda Throttles**: `Throttles > 0` over a 5-minute evaluation period.
  - **MWAA DAG Failures**: Task failure state detected via CloudWatch metric filter on MWAA worker logs (`DAG Task Failure > 0`).
  - **EMR Job Failures**: `JobRunFailed > 0` on `emr_do`.
  - **Database CPU Utilization**: `CPUUtilization > 85%` for 15 consecutive minutes on `cofig_db`.
  - **PGP Encryption Failure**: Immediate trigger on `TRANSFER_FAILED` audit event emission (fail-closed alert).

## 9. Alternatives Considered
<a id="laminar-sec-g.9"></a>
| Alternative | Why Considered | Why Rejected | Final Choice |
|---|---|---|---|
| **AWS Glue Serverless ETL** | Managed serverless Spark environment for data extractions. | Less flexible for custom declarative JSON recipes and complex multi-source joining compared to EMR Serverless; higher cold-start overhead for scheduled batch workloads. | **EMR Serverless (`emr_do`)** |
| **AWS Step Functions** | Native serverless orchestration for step-based data pipelines. | Existing enterprise blueprints and complex dependency mapping for batch parallelism strongly leverage Apache Airflow (MWAA), avoiding workflow rewrite costs. | **Amazon MWAA (`orchestrator`, `child_export_dag`, `egress dag`)** |
| **ECS Fargate Containers** | Containerized worker runtime for custom egress file processing. | Higher idle infrastructure overhead and operational complexity compared to event-driven Lambda execution for single-file egress handling. | **AWS Lambda (`egress-lambda`)** |

## 10. Appendix: Assumptions & Follow-up Question Resolution
<a id="laminar-sec-g.10"></a>
| Component | Open Question | Infrastructure Default | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|
| do-admin-api | Hosting platform not specified in diagram | ECS Fargate service behind an ALB, 1 vCPU / 2 GB task, 2 tasks min–4 max, ALB HTTPS (TLS 1.3) listener | ECS is in the SCRUM-485 allowlist; Fargate gives serverless scaling with no OS management |
| do-admin-api | JWT issuer / identity provider | JWT validated against the organisation OIDC issuer URL injected via SSM (`/laminar/dataoutbound/{env}/do-admin-api/jwks-url`) | Standard_api pattern requires bearer validation; issuer is environment config, not a new component |
| do-admin-api | Rate limiting values | Token bucket: 100 req/min per client IP at the ALB/WAF layer | Mainstream default; protects cofig_db from control-plane abuse |
| scheduler | Cron expression for the rule | `cron(0 2 * * ? *)` daily 02:00 UTC, overridable in `values.yaml` | Matches `@daily` DAG cadence; exact business time not stated in inputs |
| scheduler | Target mechanism for MWAA | EventBridge rule target = MWAA REST API via `airflow:InvokeRestApi` with input transformer building the DAG-run payload | Correct MWAA invocation path (no `CreateDagRun` IAM action exists) |
| orchestrator / child_export_dag / egress dag | One MWAA environment or three? | One MWAA environment (`laminar-dataoutbound-mwaa-{env}`) hosting all three DAGs; MWAA 2.x, Flink-less, `mw1.small` dev / `mw1.medium` staging+prod, 2 AZ private subnets | MWAA environments are per-environment, not per-DAG; DAG-level isolation via `max_active_runs = 1` per DAG |
| orchestrator / child_export_dag / egress dag | Airflow version | Airflow 2.10.x on EMR-backed MWAA | Supports dynamic task mapping and modern REST API |
| emr_do | Worker sizing within the 200-unit cap | Default pre-initialized capacity 20 vCPU / 80 GB memory; max 200 vCPU / 800 GB; Spark driver 4 vCPU/16 GB, executors 4 vCPU/16 GB each | Elastic scaling under the user-set `max_capacity_units = 200` cap; matches 1 GB / 100k-record per-customer targets |
| emr_do | Redshift access method | JDBC via Redshift Spark connector with read-only credentials from SSM over TLS | Cluster is externally owned; no IAM cross-account trust available |
| dev | Externally owned — who provisions? | Referenced only via data source / variables (`cluster_endpoint`, `database_name = dev`); never provisioned by this module | SCRUM-485 explicitly excludes n5 from the allowlist check |
| cofig_db | Backup/DR specifics | Automated backups 30-day retention, backup window 03:00–04:00 UTC, final snapshot on delete in dev; RPO 24 h / RTO 2 h | Matches stated RPO/RTO; `multi_az = false` per user decision (Recommendation: enable Multi-AZ in prod if RTO 2 h must survive AZ failure — single-AZ failover is instance-level only) |
| cofig_db | Credential management | Master credential in SSM SecureString, rotated via Secrets Manager rotation lambda outside this diagram's scope | Keeps secrets out of state and code |
| staging_bucet_internal | Lifecycle conflict (`lifecycle_enabled = false` vs 7-day purge) | Bucket-level toggle stays `false`; an explicit `Expiration` rule of exactly 7 days on `exports/*` is applied per SCRUM-486 AC#5 | Honours both the user decision and the acceptance criterion; the 30/90-day transition properties are recorded but inactive |
| staging_bucet_internal | Event notification configuration | `ObjectCreated:*` on `exports/*` → egress-lambda, with filter excluding manifest keys to avoid duplicate triggers | Prevents recursive triggering |
| egress-lambda | DLQ and retry | Async retry 2 attempts, DLQ `laminar-dataoutbound-egress-lambda-dlq-{env}` | Standard Lambda async failure handling |
| egress dag | Worker memory for 1 GB files | Streaming/chunked transfers; MWAA worker peak RSS capped < 2,048 MB per SCRUM-483 AC#2 | Memory-bounded egress tenet |
| Customer Azure Blob Destination | Auth fallback | Entra ID service principal primary; SAS token fallback only if customer cannot provision Entra ID | Per architecture document |
| Customer GCS Destination | Credential type | GCP service-account JSON key in SSM SecureString, bucket-scoped `objectCreator` role | Least-privilege cross-cloud write |
| customer SFTP server | Host-key management | Customer host key pinned in SSM at onboarding; strict verification, fail-closed | SCRUM-484 AC#2 |
| customer bucket | Cross-account write mechanism | `sts:AssumeRole` on customer-provided `CustomerCrossAccountEgressRole` with external-ID condition, account ID pinned via variable | Resolves review comment on wildcard account |
| audit_bucket | Immutability / DR | No CRR (incompatible with user's `versioning = false`); write-only IAM + Glacier tiering at 90 d; Recommendation: Object Lock compliance mode if regulatory immutability is required | Resolves review comments 6.13.2/6.13.6 without contradicting user decisions |
| All | Log retention value (SCRUM-486) | Single variable `log_retention_days` in `values.yaml` applied to every explicitly provisioned log group; value **to be confirmed with the organisation logging standard before sprint commitment** (never unset/never-expire) | The inputs do not state the value; mechanism is provisioned now |
| All | Region | `us-east-1` default, overridable in `values.yaml` | Co-location minimises latency; stated in §g.1 |
| All | Dead-letter queue permissions | Default account-level SQS resource policies (per architecture summary) | No custom DLQ resource policies required |
| All | NAT egress for MWAA/EMR | Private subnets + NAT gateway with static EIP for outbound SFTP/HTTPS to customer endpoints | Matches architecture summary; interactive shell/exec disabled via security-group egress restriction to required endpoints only |
